Correlation and p-value matrices of all pairs (pairwise complete observations)

Source: R/cor_matrix.R
cor_test_matrix.Rd

The engine always returns raw p-values; corrkit then adjusts them with stats::p.adjust() over the k(k - 1)/2 distinct pairs, as psych::corr.test() does above its diagonal.

Usage

cor_test_matrix(
  data,
  vars,
  method = "spearman",
  p_adjust = "BH",
  engine = c("auto", "psych", "correlation", "stats"),
  ci = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

data frame

vars

variables to correlate

method

correlation method (see above)

p_adjust

method of stats::p.adjust() ("BH" by default, "none" for raw p)

engine

"auto", "psych", "correlation" or "stats"

ci

confidence level of the intervals (NULL = none)

Value

object of class cor_matrix: list(r, p, p_adj, n, ci_low, ci_high, long, types, method, p_adjust, engine, ci, ci_engine); long = one row per pair (i < j) with Var1, Var2, type1, type2, r, ci_low, ci_high, p, p_adj, n.

Details

Engines (engine = "auto" picks the first available in this order):

  • Pearson / Spearman: psych::corr.test(adjust = "none"), then correlation::correlation(p_adjust = "none"), then stats::cor.test() pair by pair;

  • Kendall: correlation::correlation(), then stats::cor.test() (psych tests tau with the t formula of r, so it is not used for Kendall);

  • other methods of the correlation package ("biweight", "percentage", "blomqvist", "hoeffding", "gaussian", "shepherd", "distance"): correlation::correlation() only.

Binary variables are coded 0/1 (see as_cor_numeric()) and flagged in types.

Examples

d  <- simulate_cor_data(120)
cm <- cor_test_matrix(d, c("CRP", "IL6", "BDNF", "NfL", "BIN_CRP"), method = "spearman")
cm
#> <cor_matrix> Spearman correlations, 5 variables (1 binary), 10 pairs
#>   engine: psych::corr.test() {psych} | p adjustment: Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) over the 10 pairs | N = 112–116
#>         CRP     IL6    BDNF  NfL  BIN_CRP
#> CRP     1                                
#> IL6     0.36*** 1                        
#> BDNF    -0.16   -0.10  1                 
#> NfL     0.18    0.01   0.19  1           
#> BIN_CRP 0.87*** 0.33** -0.11 0.17 1      
head(cm$long)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 10
#>   Var1  Var2  type1      type2          r   ci_low ci_high       p     n   p_adj
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>      <chr>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 CRP   IL6   continuous contin…  0.356    0.177    0.512  1.18e-4   112 5.90e-4
#> 2 CRP   BDNF  continuous contin… -0.162   -0.342    0.0302 8.87e-2   112 1.27e-1
#> 3 IL6   BDNF  continuous contin… -0.0955  -0.281    0.0972 3.17e-1   112 3.52e-1
#> 4 CRP   NfL   continuous contin…  0.177   -0.0149   0.355  6.27e-2   112 1.25e-1
#> 5 IL6   NfL   continuous contin…  0.00784 -0.183    0.198  9.35e-1   112 9.35e-1
#> 6 BDNF  NfL   continuous contin…  0.194    0.00327  0.371  4.03e-2   112 1.01e-1
